title: Rotation by sucrose in a 20 cm tube
caption: The rotation is θ = [α]lc. With [α] = 66.5° dm⁻¹ (g/mL)⁻¹ and l = 2 dm, θ = 133° × c, a straight line through the origin. The observed 13.3° therefore gives c = 13.3/(66.5 × 2) = 0.10 g mL⁻¹; measuring the rotation is how a polarimeter reads sugar concentration.
alt: Graph of rotation in degrees against concentration in grams per millilitre: a straight line through the origin of gradient 133 degrees per gram per millilitre, passing 13.3 degrees at 0.10 grams per millilitre.
description: The horizontal axis is the concentration of sucrose in g mL⁻¹; the vertical axis is the rotation of the plane of polarisation in degrees.
θ = [α]lc = 66.5 × 2 × c = 133c, a straight line through the origin.
A measured rotation of 13.3° corresponds to c = 0.10 g mL⁻¹.
